Hi Ivan, 

We have such checks in place. 

The examples in the ticket, yes, have the same device and same phone but have never ordered together (what we call a self-order). Nothing wrong to have both a user and driver account, for most people yeah on the same device. All good until abused, or we can prove it is to be abused. 

For self-orders we have such checks: 
SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_DEVICE
SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_EMAIL
SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_NAME
SAME_RIDER_DRIVER_PHONE

And if an order happens with these parameters will be marked as fraud and we have rules that triggers if a driver hits a certain threshold of such cases.

Hi Sven,

I’ve discussed this with the UA team and for the PoC phase of this integration Bolt won’t share any data with the provider upfront - identifier that would be associated with the deposit (such as phone number) will be entered by the courier directly into the terminal. The transactions will be reported to Bolt once a day and then linked by Bolt to the specific individual. The next step will be setting up an API, so we can ping the provider’s database more often.

While this will obviously require some data transfers to be set up, in both of those use cases our provider will be acting a separate data controller and as a regulated entity will be processing data on its own behalf, therefore no additional data processing agreement is required. I’ve included additional clause in the ENG version of the agreement (11.7) to reflect this role allocation. Will also enter this new data flow into our internal records of processing activities.

Best regards,

Adriana

The updated DPA request has been attached. The police officer told me they are unable to scan the full DPA request and only sent the page with their signature on it.

The problem discussed is not related to self-orders.
In other words, the issue is as follows:
 - Driver A chooses lower tariffs.
 - Driver B opens the Rider app, sees the ride price of Driver A. Driver B thinks that Driver A dumps prices.
 - Driver B buys a one-off Sim/eSim card, installs the Rider app, and makes a fake order to Driver A.
 - Our anti-fraud system sees the rider account and device of Driver B and blocks the rider account/accounts based on the device.
 - As a result, we have blocked rider accounts of Driver B, but the driver account of Driver B is not even highlighted to us.
 - Driver B breaches our rules, and we want to identify and block - temporary or permanently - his/her +driver+ account.

So the question is as follows:

* Can we match the UID of devices of rider and driver apps of Driver B? We don’t want to make auto block rules at the moment but want to make a manual review of identified cases.

Other checks (namely, name, phone, email) is not relevant because: (1) we can do it at the moment manually with data in Admin and Looker, and (2) one-off phone number, one-off email, and fake name are used for the rider account of Driver B.

In short - credit card data can not be stored outside of card data processing scope and CS tooling *is not* our card data processing environment.

For reference - [https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/pdfs/pci_fs_data_storage.pdf|https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/pdfs/pci_fs_data_storage.pdf]

Extract from there: card number (PAN) with cardholder name, and expiration date can not be stored together *without* masking PAN.

If clients send data then this data should be either permanently deleted or irreversibly masked.

Masking: _Mask PAN when displayed (the first six and last four digits are the maximum number of digits to be displayed), such that only personnel with a legitimate business need can see the full PAN.  This requirement relates to protection of PAN displayed on screens, paper receipts, printouts, etc., and is not to be confused with Requirement 3.4 for protection of PAN when stored in files, databases, etc._

*Impact on CS Tickets:*

For these 3 markets we’ve noticed an increase of total tickets opened by drivers & also the increase of resolution time by CS members for the month of December. The total ticket count increased 30% (from 150k tickets in Nov to 190k tickets in Dec). The top 5 issues were:

|#|Issue|# Tickets|% from total|% MoM|
|1|I have a question about driver debt|35,094|31.94%|262.28%|
|2|Rider didn't pay for their trip|22,896|20.84%|26.02%|
|3|My account has been blocked|19,002|17.30%|2.41%|

Hi [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] \!

So the main question is which legal basis to rely for sharing the driver leads contact details to Fleets. I scheduled a call with you [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] to go through the alternatives to make a scalable decision based on the following: 

# *Consent*
In essence this would be the most straightforward basis to rely because the leads have a free choice whether they would like to forward their details in order to be contacted by the Fleets. 
Has its downsides:
- we have to keep the logs on the consents given;
- data subject always has the opportunity to withdraw their consent - should be as easy as giving the consent (how would this be managed, how would the fleets be notified about the consent withdrawal etc);
- can we provide the details of all fleet partners who the data will be forwarded in the consent form?

But in general - from legal perspective → doable. 
# *Processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract*
The processing should be objectively necessary for the performance of the contract. 
The controller should be able to demonstrate how the main object of the specific contract with the data subject cannot, as a matter of fact, be performed if the specific processing of the personal data in question does not occur.

It is not objectively necessary for the performance of the agreement to provide lead details to fleets. It is necessary to have a vehicle, but the lead has the opportunity to reach out to fleets themselves, find a vehicle by other ways etc. Also it is not 100% guaranteed that even if we would provide the leads contact details to fleets this would result an agreement between them and therefore ensure the lead with a vehicle in the end.

I think this basis would not be appropriate. 
# *Legitimate interest*

For this we would need to conduct a further legitimate interest assessment. We would also need to update our driver pp with this processing activity (among other things of course). 

All in all - the strongest legal basis for this case seems to be consent. Legitimate interest can be argued - depending on the set up this may be the most scalable solution. So lets discuss the details over a call.

same, because we are holding block->lock or the block is
not accessible by other threads (BUF_BLOCK_REMOVE_HASH),
or the index is not accessible to other threads
(buf_fix_count == 0 when DROP TABLE or similar is executing
buf_LRU_drop_page_hash_for_tablespace()).

In the buf_LRU_drop_page_hash_for_tablespace function,
buff_pool will be required by LRU_list_mutex
Start scan for dirty pages.

Also AHI entries will be removed at this point.{noformat}

3.If buffer_pool_size is large No.2 process takes time and because buff_pool is required by LRU_list_mutex any other threads can't access the buffer_pool at this point.

4.When the scan is completed, tablespace will be purged from the filesystem.

{noformat}Ext4 or ZFS does not delete the file itself right away, it removes the inodes from the file in order to reduce the IO operation.
However, if the the tablespace is huge, removing inodes takes time.{noformat}

5.When tablespace is purged, the lock will be released.

*How to avoid the stall situation? 1.  Minimize I/O operation.* 

This solution is simple and very efficient. 

Create a hardlink to the target tablespace and remove a file descriptor rather than inodes. 

When the Linux kernel deletes a file and if the file has a hardlink, it won't remove inodes. Instead, it only removes the file descriptor used for the removal operation. 

1. Create a hardlink to the target tablespace 

2. EXECUTE DROP TABLE DDL and MySQL instance will only remove file descriptor and void I/O bottleneck

Hi, atm we don’t provide the user with a “cancel” button during the pre-authorization phase. Here the app displays a spinning loader and the user is stuck on that. To prevent this from being a dead-end for the user we have a timeout on our side (delivery), where we cancel the booking if that time passes with no result.

This can happen in 2 cases, I believe:
1. the user finishes the challenge, we get a confirmation from the app that it’s ready to show the active order screen, but we don’t get any event from the Payments regarding the booking. This is useful especially if the Payments service is down.
2. the user finishes the challenge, we get a successful event from Payments, but we don’t get a confirmation from the app that it’s ready to show the active order screen. This is useful when the app loses track of the booking and we want to prevent creating an order without showing it to the user.
These payouts have been finished now.

Hi Tomek,
As I understand you want to get some data out of Redshift into Google Drive (or maybe google sheet?).

From what we do have atm, I see few things that could be used as building blocks:

h4. Alternative 1

1. Airflow for scheduling Redshift Unload query, to unload query result to S3 as CSV.
2. We have one solution set as S3 CSV → Google Sheets set up. It uses AWS lambda triggered by S3 notification, so each time a new CSV is uploaded to S3 (in this case it comes from Workday Adaptive Insights export) it is triggered and loads data from CSV into Google Sheets.

The thing with that is it will require quite involved setup, S3 buckets, IAM policies, etc. Also as this is one use case ‘solution’ we do not have any docs, etc. here.

h4. Alternative 2

Python code doing Redshift query and writing file to Google Sheet/Drive, in memory, run in container, on AWS Batch, orchestrated with Airflow. This will require implementing all the stuff in Python (query, transformation + using google`s SDKs to save the thing at destination), but is more coherent and easier to setup. 
Quite involved manual is prepared [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/2336850029/Python+jobs+with+Airflow+and+Batch]. 
If data volumes are manageable, you could probably also use plain Airflow DAG and code, without the AWS Batch and containerizing your code.

h4. Other options

Similarly to 2 Spark job could be used, but this is significant overshoot. We are also in progress of Databricks rollout, so a Notebook to report the data + store it to Google at the end, could do the work, it has also scheduling options, so even Airflow could be omitted. We shall have some things rolled-out to experiments, soon. Although we have not planned how it would work for such cases like yours (in terms of usage patterns), yet. 

----

None of the solutions is simple, but these are all options you would achieve your end goal with (with some coding on the way).

The only way a liability like this will become transferable will be to significantly manage the frequency and severity of the possible losses.

Hi\!

Please see the answer below. If you have any additional questions, please let me know and I will reply swiftly.



+Dress code (Smart casual, no open-toe footwear and competitor branding/colours etc)+ 

*Answer:* overall, this idea can be implemented. We can set the dress code, but the small risk remains that we should provide the clothing. This could be regulated in the internal rules (of procedure).

Note: if the occupational health check-up demands some PPE, we must bear the costs for that.

+·       Minimum Acceptance rate: 90%+

+·       Minimum Completion rate: 98%+

*Answer*: if this is part of employment and can be grounds for dismissal, the rules and procedures should be very clearly set out. An employee can be dismissed if they breach our set-out rules, given that the rules are reasonable.

PS\! As this can be grounds for dismissal, the internal rules should be very-well thought through – if there is a network error? If the person was bound for a rest break? Any grounds for dismissal should be given extra attention – courts and labor dispute committees usually rule in favor of the employee.

+·       100% compliance to assigned shift schedules+ 

+·       Shift schedules attached+ [+here+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dSXaapziRdtARYhr53yIfEnR9Too4g8-j2qlzCvNxzA/edit] 

 *Answer:* Shifts can be implemented, and the calculation can be up to 4 months.

Note: when planning the shifts, we must pay additional attention to the night shifts – there are some additional limitations and rules for night-time employees. Breaching the night-time limitations can be grounds for administrative proceedings for the employer (and potential PR risk).

+·       Indefinite working terms subject to notice period being served if wished to resign+

*Answer*: This is set by the law. We cannot have shorter notice periods than stated in the Employment Contracts Act – during the probation period 15 days for the employer and employee. The agreement can be terminated for convenience only by the employee – giving us 30-day notice.

PS\! Employer can terminate the employment the agreement but is bound by limitations. As a general rule – a warning must be given to the employee before terminating the employment and notice periods adhered to (15/30/60/90 days – depending on the seniority).

 

+·       If renting a car, to use Bolt selected partners+

+·       If owning a car, to ensure it fulfills Bolt vehicle requirements+ 

*Answer:* Car is something they are using for employment and as this is considered equipment necessary for fulfilling the contract, +it should be provided by the employer+. If not provided by the employer, we still have the responsibility to ensure that the car is safe and sound. In employment context, think of the car as another equipment on the premises – if we don’t know/evaluate the risks associated with the use of personal car for fulfilling the employment agreement, we could become responsible for accidents and personal injuries.

PS\! The risk here is regarding the disputes related to personal injuries – the employer is held responsible for almost all instances: failing to inspect the equipment, failing to give the proper training, failing to create safe working environment. The worst case scenario (if not covered by the insurance) – we must pay the injured person until the end of their life.

PS\! Also, another look should be taken from insurance PoV – are all the cars covered by our current insurance policy? Or are there any exclusions?

 

+·       Must have GPS assisted mobile device for Bolt driver app to be fully functional+ 

*Answer:* as this is working equipment, this mobile device should be provided by us. We could have BYOD policy (in the internal rules). We also should provide the telecommunications services (Telia/Elisa/Tele2).

 

·       To ensure close to 100% success as and when Bolt applies for service card/ride-hailing relevant licences for individuals, individuals need to ensure they are X years old, have no criminal record etc etc 

*Answer:* The rules for applying for the service card is set in the Public Transportation Act. Short summary: you must have B-cat driver’s license and good reputation. The criteria for good reputation is set in the law. If we want to have deviations from the applicable law, there should be grounds for it, it should be reasonable criteria and the less damaging approach should be picked – otherwise it could be regarded as discrimination.

TL;DR: if person has record for causing personal injury, drunk driving, speeding 41+ km/h, endangering pedestrians and other vehicles and the record has not been archived, the person does not have a good reputation.

We can cancel the employment contract if we find out that the employee does not meet the criteria set out and they have given us partial/falsified data.

 

+·       Employees have the option of working longer hours, subject that the working and rest time regulations are met, if there’s a bonus available during their shift days, these bonuses are subjected to conditions and changes+ 

*Answer:* +employer is responsible for controlling and organizing the worktime+. If we allow uncontrolled setting of worktime, we can have risk of paying additional overtime. We cannot delegate our responsibility to the employee as we will be held responsible for keeping the schedules. Different rules apply to employees and contractors – employees must have 11 hours of consecutive rest time. And the rest time can alter if the employee works during the night.

Also, working during the night-time is subject to 125% fee if the wage is lower than 815,70 EUR.

Depending on the approach, we must pay out over-time either EoM or EoP. Overtime is paid out at least 150% rate. Any payments made to the employee will be basis for PTO calculation. Giving free time is more preferred option as the cost for company is 100%, not 150%.

Additional bonuses can be applied, given that they are temporary and thus not becoming a part of the employment contract. If we say for using personal car for employment, we shall pay you 400 EUR extra and decide to change the approach, if could have become a part of the employment contract - and any worsening or changing conditions is the will of the parties, not the will of the employer.

 

+·       Employees are not allowed to work for competitors during the employment period+

*Answer:* this can be set in the employment contract, but we have to narrow the scope and aim of the restriction. We can state (in the intel rules) that the employee must be online during working hour and dedicate their full time to the employer (and not work for Yandex during the working hours).

This can be in the employment contract, but we must regulate the conditions in internal documents binding to the employee.

 

+·       In the event that employment period is terminated, employees are not allowed to work for competitors X months after date of termination+ 

*Answer:* this can be set, if we are protecting a business secret and we are paying for it. No restriction after the end of the employment agreement is valid if we are not paying for it. That means, if we restrict competition, we must pay for the restriction in proportion how much it limits employee’s life. Even if we can find a business secret to protect, it is costly and most likely cannot be enforced. If the base salary is 800 EUR and state minimum is 653 EUR, the minimum we are talking about is 82% of the base fee per month for the duration of the limitation. +Short answer: cannot be implemented+.

 

+·       Employees are allowed to make the transition to a Bolt independent driver after a minimum of 3 months service in the employment period with 1 month’s notice period+  

*Answer:* Contractor and employment agreements can be valid at the same time. We cannot give any additional conditions in the employment agreement regarding the ending the agreement besides those stated by the law. We can always terminate the employment agreement based on the will of the parties.

 

+·       Attending a Bolt training/onboarding session is compulsory+ 

*Answer:* employer is responsible for proper introduction and safety trainings. Employer must ensure that the employees have their medical evaluation done in the first 4 months of employment.

NB\! We must provide the employees OHAS training\! Including safety rules on the road.

Hi [~accountid:610d3190ae72b2006f81ee2e], according to the advice received by the external counsel, Bolt is obliged to provide uniforms for pickers in order to ensure health and safety of pickers and to ensure cleanliness in the food-handling area. Therefore, the badge would not be a sufficient solution.

Please find the comprehensive answer by the external counsel below. Please let me know in case of any further questions.

_____



Pursuant to the applicable legislation (namely, the Portuguese Labour Code and the Regime for the Promotion of Occupational Safety and Health - Law no. 102/2009), employees have the right to work in conditions that respect their safety and health.

 

The responsibility for protecting the health and safety of employees lies with their employer or, if applicable, with the person, individual or collective, that manages the facility at which business activities are carried out.

 

The employers (or, if applicable, the abovementioned persons) must ensure employee safety and health in all aspects of their work and must ensure, on a continuous and permanent basis, the exercise of their work activities in conditions which are safe and healthy for the employee, considering several general principles of prevention, including the avoidance of risks.

 

Prevention measures may include the provision of personal protective equipment (“PPE”) to protect employees against risks to their safety and health. The PPE (which may include gloves, uniforms, safety footwear, etc.) must comply with the standards applicable to their design and manufacture in terms of safety and health, be appropriate to the risks to be prevented and the conditions existing in the workplace, without in itself implying an increase in risk, meeting the ergonomic and health requirements of the employee and being suitable for its user.

 

The employer (or, if applicable, the abovementioned persons) must provide PPE when it is required and ensure it is functioning properly. Employers must provide and keep available in the workplace adequate information about each type of PPE and inform employees of the risks against which PPE aims to protect them. They must provide training on the use of PPE and organize, if necessary, safety exercises.

 

In this case, considering that the temporary workers (staff employed by the employment agency) are providing work for Bolt and at Bolt’s premises, the responsibility for protecting their health and safety lies with Bolt, including the obligation to provide personal protective equipment.

 

Regarding the use of uniforms, pursuant to Regulation (EC) no. 852/2004, of the European Parliament and of the Council, of 29 April 2004, on the hygiene of foodstuffs: “_every person working in a food-handling area is to maintain a high degree of personal cleanliness and is to wear suitable, clean and, where necessary, protective clothing_” (chapter VIII – Personal Hygiene).

 

Complementarily, under the [Good Personal Hygiene Practices for food-handlers|https://www.asae.gov.pt/perguntas-frequentes1/higiene-pessoal.aspx], of the portuguese Authority for Economic and Food Safety (ASAE), the working clothing shall be suitable for the job and for exclusive use inside the workplace.

 

Therefore, considering that the use of protective clothing by the staff providing work at Bolt’s premises is necessary to guarantee their safety and health at work, and, thus, may constitute a PPE, it is Bolt’s responsibility to provide such equipment.

Hey David, strictly from the legal perspective the disclaimer where we use the language like “by doing A you agree to B“ theoretically is imposing higher risk than the wording proposed below as this may be deemed as non-compliant consent under the GDPR. In principal, GDPR sets out 6 possible grounds for processing - consent and legitimate interest are being 2 of them. As those legal grounds are alternative and not complementary to each other, if we decide to go with legitimate interest, no consent-like wording is required.

* *Desired outcome* - the project will last throughout the year, so I would suggest changing the 1st outcome from “by the end of the project” to “by the end of the round of listening sessions”. Unless you aim at having only 1 growth need throughout the whole year 🙂

Some feedback:

* I would rename the problem statement into opportunity statement. Based on what you have written, it is not a problem we solve but an opportunity we capitalise on.
* *Desired outcomes* - I would suggest to have the specific target under Success metrics. Plus, for Bootcamps we actually aim at much higher than 20% of participants getting roles. Based on our discussion during planning day in December, we agreed on 60% target 🙂 
** Like I explained in the previous project plan - increase in number of agents applying means nothing. Yes, role is popular but if none of them actually get the role - what does it matter? 🙂 
** At least 1 ambassador in each region is also a success metric for diversity of the program. In this case, try to reword what you want to achieve here - e.g. making the program diverse, or diversifyin growth opportunities in CS.
* *Deliverables*
** At least one new team collaboration is rather a success metric for broadening the scope of the program.
** Ambassadors are a product of the first deliverable
** What would be the post-program collaboration? Deliverables should be tangible and all of them contributing to the overall success of the program. In this case, will the program fail if we do not collaborate with the participants after the program? If not, then it is a nice-to-have that can be merged with something else.
* *Out of scope*
** Don’t we provide teams with guidelines? e.g. monthly reports. If not, why do we expect them? If we expect them, does the aligned format matter?
* *Stakeholders*
** Would you rather work with RLs here or still with STLs?
* *Success metrics*
** Like before, let’s add the target for each.
* *Timeline*
** You can think of an approximate timeline considering the stakeholders you have in mind for the Q1-Q2.

h3. [Police DPA Requests|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3572172096/The+United+Kingdom+and+Ireland#Police-DPA-Requests]

*Escalating DPAs to Case Managers*

All police-related tickets like *Police* *DPA requests* will have to be escalated via Slack channel #uk-potentiallycriminal-events:

* Escalate the Zendesk ticket to UK&Ireland:Requests from Authorities Zendesk queue;
* Choose lighting emoji from the bottom left-hand corner on Slack #uk-potentiallycriminal-events;
* Enter the Zendesk ticket link;
* In case of a missing person, abduction, or an ongoing crime investigation case, add {{URGENT}} to the subject line.
* Tag [@casemanagers|https://taxify.slack.com/admin/user_groups] when posting a case to get them to action the tickets.

*Escalating Urgent DPAs During Weekends and Workdays (Outside of Working Hours)*

An urgent DPA is a DPA regarding a life or death situation, such as a live missing person, a terrorism threat, and/or urgent medical emergency. Anything that does not cause an imminent risk to life (such as an ongoing investigation into drug supply) is not considered urgent.

* Before 9 pm UK time , post the case via the workflow as stated above. If there is no response within one hour, call the Case Manager [on call|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10QDQneWuenL55efcySj9dNEu2_5RzrCTfwYD4VnkB6w/edit#gid=0] for the weekend.

* During the night between 12 am and 9 am UK time, post the case via the workflow as stated above. The DPA will be actioned as soon as possible. There is no need to call the Case Managers. If it’s extremely urgent, the police would call in. ⬇️ 
* If the police reach out by phone due to urgency, follow the procedure [Urgent Data Requests in Life and Death Situations|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3572172096/The+United+Kingdom+and+Ireland#Urgent-Data-Requests-in-Life-and-Death-Situations].

{panel}

Structure which repeats all the levels of the key parts allows you to create a key which both has a string value as well as a bunch of child key-value pairs. Whereas object-like structure allows you only to have either of one: either string OR a bunch of child keys.

And migrating to object like structure will force us to change the key with the string value and replace it throughout the module codebase (plz see the screen shot). 

We definitely have inconsistency issue in this file, but IMO we need to discuss and agree which structure we should use and stick to it.

In general - individuals have the right to access and receive a copy of their personal data. We as a controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing. So as long we are holding data in an identifiable format connected to the user, then we should provide this. 

The current export we have - most likely (as we have seen with this case as well) doesn’t include all the personal data we should actually be able to provide as a controller. So therefore if something is not included in the export (but is still asked by the data subject), doesn’t mean that we automatically refuse to provide the data. 

Geolocation data associated with an account constitutes personal data of the account holder. For scooter rides - there is no exemption to rely on why not to provide the data. 

So providing GPS co-ordinates with timestamps of the ride for example in a CSV format is okay.

A good rule of thumb is 10 working days.
Pre-auths for successfully captured payments are released immediately by Bolt’s payment provider but this can take the individual bank a couple of days depending on their specific processes. 

For failed payments, (technical and temporary errors especially) there might be an issue with the transaction and the pre-auth is stuck. Normally banks cancel such pre-auths if transactions fail but we have exceptions. 

If a failed payment pre-auth exceeds 10 working days, a ticket can be sent to payments service desk to check the status with our provider and escalate. 

However, if the payment is successful, always advise users to follow up with their banks as we have limited control over such incidents.

h5. The issue appeared because:

* Keyword is entered or top tag pressed so {{SearchInput}} becomes visible
* When user presses 1st time on Search tab {{hideSearchInput}} is called
* When user presses 2nd time on Search tab {{showSearchInput}} is called (but hide animation has not yet ended)
* Now hide animation ends and triggers {{setIsVisible(false)}} which means that {{SearchInput}} is hidden and remains hidden (even though {{shouldShow}} is true)

h5. The solution:

* Always in case {{shouldShow}} is true, set {{isVisible}} to true as well 
(Even if hide animation ends and sets the {{isVisible}} to false then it will be set back to true since {{shouldShow}} is true)

As for simplifying the content with the help of other tools, I believe these are options we can utilise:

#  *Jump-to links in combination with better utilisation of* [*white space*|https://uxplanet.org/the-power-of-whitespace-a1a95e45f82b]
See [this KB article in Beehive|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/internal/360021415640] as an example - more white space between the H3 section content could make it less overwhelming on the eye.
# *Use different formatting for Step titles and sub-scenarios within a step (achieve a better hierarchy of the article content structural elements with different formatting options)*
Right now, both are formatted in bold. Take the same KB article as an example - since both the Step titles and the sub-scenarios are highlighted in bold, at a glance it might not be clear which highlighted elements to direct attention to first. Of course, our current CS agents know how the KB articles are built (their structure). However, this might make it more difficult for a new joiner to understand and learn the content of the article.
# *Separate KB articles that cover multiple sub-processes (so that each sub-process is covered in a separate article)*
If we go this route, we could use the following formatting: headings for Step titles, bold for sub-scenario titles and for highlighting important bits of text in the bulleted lists. It looks like it’s a popular option for Help Center sites (see [Wix|https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-editor-unable-to-select-an-element] and [Squarespace|https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/205812378] for example).
However, we need to evaluate whether having 10 separate articles instead of all 10 processes covered in a single umbrella article would be a better solution *for the CS agents*.

There might be other formatting options we could use. However, I believe that all of this also warrants the need for proper research to determine a solid way of how we want the articles to look. And then - discuss with the CS Product team so they can evaluate how we can achieve the desired look with the least development resource requirements.

Regarding the driver cancelation, we have 2 different states for cancelling rides that can happen before the driver is driving with the rider:

{{no_driver_provided}} and {{client_did_not_show}}

If the driver cancels the order before accepting we will keep looking for another driver, so it is transparent for the rider and we do not need to send an SMS. 
But if we cannot find any (other) driver, the order will go on the “no_driver_provided” state and we will send an SMS, if the order came from a scheduled order.

The change here is that we are going to send this SMS for all on-demand orders now, with a small change to the text.
Existing message:
{{Unfortunately, there are no drivers available at your location. Please find an alternate method of transport.}}
New message:
{{Unfortunately, there are no drivers available at your location. Please rebook}}


When the driver cancels a ride after accepting it is a different thing. First the driver needs a reason for it and we will sometimes require the driver to wait for some time before being able to cancel it, or write a text with the reason why the ride is being cancelled (see image attached).

In the end all these cancellation reasons are mapped to a “client_did_not_show” and we don’t send any SMS for it.
I think we need an specific message for it, something like:
{{Unfortunately, you ride was cancelled <should we tell the reason?>. Please rebook}}

Just an internal note on the process, so we can potentially avoid these things happening in the future:

When workers have job changes, there is a possibility that they might be moved to a different position in HCM module.

Each worker has a 1:1 relationship with positions, and if a worker gets promoted then they can usually stay in the same position but upgrade the job profile and relevant compensation - this means that all security roles that were previously assigned stay with same position. 

However, in some scenarios workers may move to different positions - e.g. a new position is available on the team, or a different team then a task that’s there as part of the job change is for a Role Maintainer to review (add/remove/keep) roles or transfer them to a new position.

* The option to call will be disabled entirely in the following conditions:

*What impact is early cash out having on debt accumulation?*

Checking the numbers the total debt increased by 0.5% per day in December on average for the 3 markets. From Dec data we can see that on average +4% debt was accumulated during the weekend (vs the week). We can see that a portion of the debt is repaid by drivers on Tuesday/Wednesday but on average only 1% is paid back during the week hence the total debt was slowly accumulating throughout the month. Within the month the total debt increased by ~350k EUR from 2.1M to 2.5M (+16%). Looking at the yearly numbers we’re noticing total debt starting accumulating from the end of Nov 2021 - it was relatively constant sitting around 1.5M EUR across the year but in about a month increased to ~2M EUR (~30% increase).

!Screenshot 2022-01-31 at 12.02.47.png|width=1069,height=511!

In total 2.5M EUR (-18% MoM) was successfully transferred via early cashouts during Dec for the 3 markets. We’re noticing an increase in cashout requests on Fridays & also the sum is more than tripled each Friday compared with Monday the same week. It could be because some drivers aren’t planning to work during the weekend but it also might lead to debt accumulation for the following few days. From the few data points for December we can see that actually early cash out on Friday & debt accumulation over the weekend are in positive correlation (R = 0.89) meaning that bigger cashout on Friday leads to larger debt increase over the weekend/Monday. From the 4 weeks in December we can see that for the 3 markets roughly the same amount has been 1) sent via early cash outs on Fridays (420k EUR) & 2) debt increased the following Monday (380k EUR).

** It’s unclear for ticket requesters how to select the priority correctly - they end up selecting something that doesn’t actually represent the urgency of the change requested in the ticket.
** As a result, I end up not referring to the Priority set by the ticket request and simply evaluate the request change urgency myself and plan it accordingly to my current and future sprint plans.
* *Article update:*
** Can we change it to _Related KB article_? Sometimes the requester doesn’t insert the article URL - not sure if they may just forget it though, perhaps specifying to list the related article may help
* *Ticket link:*
** Very often not included or requester includes a random ticket just to submit the form. Tickets are also often in EE or RU - I can surely translate them but it may be useful to indicate for the requester to provide context if the ticket example is not in English 

*My suggestions:*

* For _non-effective or incorrect process_, we could replace _Why is this needed_ text field with these two - *Issue with the current process* and *Suggested process*:
** This could help the requester provide information on both the issue and how they see the process update.
** If they are unsure about it (which can happen when they submit a request for a process that we’re thinking of way ahead of time), they can simply state that they have no proposition yet and want to discuss this)
* We had a field for a due date - but it’s not there for the _Non-effective or incorrect process_ type of a request. It would help if we nudge the requester to think about when they would like to see the change launched - and if they don’t have a due date to share, they can say that 

Hope this helps\! I’ll also share in the thread a checklist I shared with the Drive CS leads to help them also prepare the SD request nicely 

*Checklist for CS - what kind of information helps me work on process change requests*

* *Is there alignment between CS<>OPS in regards to the desired process update outcome?* The main driver for me asking to review a process is lack of confidence. It usually stems from either me not being sure if I know all the contributing details, or if there’s a lack of consensus of the desired process update outcome. For the latter, it is most often when OPS team’s take on the process update is different from how CS see it. The better aligned we are before requesting a process change, the more confident I also feel with the final process change.
* *Are all relevant context details, especially undocumented ones, shared on the SD ticket?* While I can see the existing content and other resources, sharing knowledge that is not documented anywhere greatly helps me understand how the current process works, where the problem is, and what is the desired outcome.
* *Does the process change request come from user feedback and inquiries?* How many tickets do we receive with this issue? Sharing this data, or at least an estimation helps me evaluate the priority against other content tasks for Drive.
* *Does the SD ticket mention who is the SME/POC for the topic?* This ensures that I reach out to the right person to get confirmation or additional details, especially if the SME is someone other than the ticket requester.
* *Is there a due date for when you’d wish the change to be in effect?* If there is no particular due date, you can state that as well. I still evaluate the priority of the ticket against the rest of the tasks I have, but providing a rough due date (if there is one) helps me prioritise tasks correctly.

I guess the question is if you would see this as a potential risk of being in breach of GDPR art 22. 

Long story short:

* Fraud team will do automatic fraud scoring of driver pay-outs (currently manual)
** IF suspicious pay-out: Fraud team will do manual review. And may thus delay planned pay-out by 24hrs.
*** IF clear fraud - BLOCK
*** IF suspicious - warning and some limitations (like cash trips) for awhile
*** IF nothing - no action
** IF clear fraud - no review, auto block of account (clear fraud defined super-narrowly a clear pattern of fraud with no prior usage of Bolt or any good-trip data).

From legal side:

*  Pay outs delayed by 24 hrs IF suspicious. Could cause issues with our contractual obligation to pay-out funds. BUT in most markets we are covered as our contracts do not commit to clear pay-out date and in most cases we may be flexible.
* IF suspicious - actions taken do not trigger requirements of special notice, etc. And simple transparent (aka Notification via email/in-app about how has been screened? what irregularity found? what actions taken?) would cover most of legal risk
** [~accountid:5b7bea06cd0cc72a612c975f]  let’s work on a notification / transparency framework so that ever time there is any effect on the driver - we play open and transparent. Ideally in future we would also be transparent around 24hr suspicion and would give heads up that is happening and why.
* IF Fraud - actions taken by Bolt are rather “severe”. And would normally trigger requirements to notify in advance. However, our FRAUD definition is conservative and risk of false positives is very very low. So in great majority of the cases people blocked under this rule would be in clear breach of our T&Cs (normally there is a specific rule around fraud block) as well as a potential criminal activity as well. These cases are always exempted from in-advance notices, etc (e.g P2B). So legally not worried about any additional safeguards. But transparency as always - would be welcome. E.g. in a form of email informing about fraudulent activity and block to use Bolt platform.

_So in short:_ we do have good legal grounds to suspend pay-outs + to block accounts engaged in fraud. No extra steps needed from legal besides the following:

 a) transparency +

b) cross-check of local T&Cs on the pay-out frequency (and ability to have a 24hr delay) when launching markets

Therefore, we also suggest to delete such references in the commercial proposal (since it is intended to form part of the agreement) and amend it accordingly to the wording used in Clause 1 paragraphs 1 and 2 of the service agreement.



*_b)_*             *Financial proposal / price (p. 11 and 12)*

Bolt should confirm if it agrees with the amounts stated in the financial proposal. Nevertheless, please note that it refers to additional fees for overtime work and the payment of premium (_prémio_). Kelly should clarify to what this premium refers to.

Furthermore, in the list of the amounts not included in the price (p. 12), there is a typo / incomplete sentence which does not allow us to understand what is at stake (“_…n.º 6 do Código do Trabalho_”). Kelly should clarify this reference.

 On the other hand, the proposal states that the price includes the +compensation for precarious employment+ (_compensação de precariedade the emprego_). Kelly should also clarify to what this compensation refers to. Please note that +Kelly (and not Bolt) is, as the employer, liable for the payment of the legal compensation in case of termination+ of the employment contracts of the employees allocated to the services. Therefore, if this wording refers to compensation for employment contract’s termination, it should not be accepted. Otherwise, it increases the risk already identified of considering that Bolt is the _de facto_ employer of the employees allocated to the services.



*_c)_*             *Future application of the proposal’s terms and conditions (p. 13, paragraph 3)*

Please note that the proposal’s general terms and conditions state that they will apply to future service agreements entered into between Kelly and Bolt regarding the same type of services in the next 12 months (unless otherwise agreed between the parties). We leave this aspect to your consideration.

 

*_d)_*             *Delay in payment (p. 13, paragraph 8)*

The proposal states that if the price is not paid by Bolt in time, the latter will have to pay it plus interest and plus a minimum amount of € 40.00 for compensation for collection costs. This is not stated in the service agreement and, therefore, Bolt should confirm if agrees with this.

 

*_e)_*             *Non-execution of the services because of Bolt (p. 13, paragraph 9)*

The proposal states that if Bolt prevents the execution of the services, by action or omission, namely by non-complying with its obligations, will be liable for the payment of the total price as the services had been provided. We recommend to add the following exception: _“...except if the execution of the services is not possible due to majeure force reasons_”. This exception aims to protect Bolt of having to pay the price to Kelly when the non-execution of the services was not caused by Bolt’s fault (_e.g._ causes related to Coronavirus).

 

*_f)_*              *Clients’ portfolio of Kelly (p. 13, paragraph 14)*

The proposal states that, unless otherwise communicated (in writing) by Bolt, the latter accepts that Kelly will include Bolt’s name and/or logotype, and synopsis of the developed project, in the Clients’ portfolio of Kelly, for reference of its commercial offer, up to a maximum of 2 years following the termination of the service agreement. For this purpose, Bolt will have to send to Kelly its company logo, after the acceptance of the proposal. This is not stated in the service agreement and, therefore, Bolt should confirm if agrees with this.

 

*_g)_*             *Audits (p. 13, paragraph 18)*

The proposal states that Bolt should comply with Kelly's security policies and standards including the Privacy Statement and that, for this purpose, Kelly will carry out an audit (one per service agreement in force) which will be charged to Bolt according to the number of hours estimated to do such audit. This represents an additional cost (not stated in the service agreement) for Bolt which should, therefore, confirm if agrees with it.

 

*_h)_*            *Limitation of Kelly’s liability (p. 14, paragraph 28)*

The proposal states that Kelly will be responsible for the damages caused in case of non-compliance with the service agreement, including in case of willful misconduct or negligence of its employees, up to the amount Kelly is entitled to receive as the price for the full term of the agreement in which the circumstance giving rise to the damage occurred. We had already suggested to delete a similar limitation from the service agreement (which stated “_up to the price agreed between the parties_”) because it is not protective of Bolt’s interest. We do not recommend such a threshold, but it is a matter of commercial nature, rather than legal and therefore we leave the acceptance or not of this liability limitation to your consideration (as we left it for the service agreement).

 

*_i)_*              *Non-solicitation obligation (p. 14, paragraph 33)*

The proposal states that during the service agreement and in the 2 years following its termination, Bolt cannot hire or recommend to third parties Kelly’s employees assigned to the provision of the services (unless otherwise agreed in writing between the parties). In addition, it states that in case of non-compliance with this obligation, Bolt will pay to Kelly a compensation correspondent to the gross amounts paid to the employee at stake in the 24 months prior to his/her termination, plus the costs that Kelly has incurred with his/her selection, hiring and training.

 

Although it is common to include in the agreements, the external counsel confirmed that this type of obligations is not valid under Portuguese law since it corresponds to a limitation to the freedom of work principle and, therefore, it is not enforceable. Nevertheless, we recommend to deleted at least the Bolt’s obligation of paying a compensation to Kelly in such terms since it is something that is being agreed between the parties (not affecting the employee) and, thus, may be considered a valid obligation. We consider that it is too onerous for Bolt, but we leave to your consideration.

 

*_j)_*              *Document “**_Pedido de Elementos de Identificação_* *(point B)*

Please note that in the document “_Pedido de Elementos de Identificação_” (point B paragraph 1 b)) and regarding the time and place of the services, it is stated “to be defined”. However, these matters are expressly stated in the service agreement and, therefore, this wording should be replaced by the following: “_According to the service agreement_” (_Conforme contrato_).

As to the addendum in respect of data protection matters, please note that the provisions set out in the data protection addendum provided by Kelly are related with international personal data transfers. However, the data protection clause included in the service agreement covers the processing of personal data made by Kelly on behalf of Bolt under the terms of article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation (“*GDPR*”) which already covers the international data transfers matter. Moreover, the addendum does not (_i_) indicate Kelly as a processor of personal data in accordance with data protection regulation and (_ii_) include the main requirements established in article 28 of the GDPR. Therefore, we believe that data protection addendum provided by Kelly should be disregarded considering that this matter is already governed by the service contract in a more complete and accurate manner.

Finally, note that the service agreement states that the minimum team composition is stated in the Single Annex, but from the proposal it is not clear how many of Kelly’s employees will be allocated to the services. This should be clarified with Kelly.

+In light of the above, we believe that these documents submitted by Kelly should not be included as an annex to the service agreement, considering that, in general, the provisions established in such documents are not in line with the provisions in the body of the service agreement.+

+Instead, we believe that the so-called+ +_Single Annex_+ +of the service agreement should be properly prepared and should include solely the information specifically intended to be included in the same as provided for in the body of the service agreement and which corresponds to the criteria to determine the price, the team composition and profiles.+

*How many drivers were affected? For how many days?*

We see a linear growth in active & total drivers for these markets throughout the year. Looking at the blocking rates MoM we can see that rate’s slowly decreased from 20% in Jan 2021 to 14% in Nov 2021 & then raised again in December. In December there were ~560k total drivers (+10% MoM) & ~202k active drivers (+7% MoM). From the total drivers, 111k (~20%) were cash-blocked hence we can estimate ~40k active drivers were cash-blocked in December.

!Screenshot 2022-02-01 at 10.25.47.png|width=1078,height=504!

Looking at the numbers in more detail we can see that the cash-blocking rates started to increase from the 26th Nov (10.12% cash-blocked), the blocking rates peaked at the 20th Dec (13.45% cash-blocked) and return to ‘normal’ on the 16th January 2022 (10.07% cash-blocked). So in general the high cash-blocking rates for the 3 markets lasted for *51 days*. 

!Screenshot 2022-02-01 at 10.47.00.png|width=1075,height=512!

After double checking the number of affected drivers as the period lasted >1 month, I noticed the volume doubled to ~400k active drivers but the rate of cash-blocked drivers stayed the same at 20%. Hence the total number of active cash-blocked drivers were ~80k for the whole period. So we can assume roughly *40k drivers* became inactive in December due to being cash-blocked.

Hola Larry\!

A bit of background information, the fraud team manages the financial risk of our clients.
We mainly try to reduce the amount of money we get in chargebacks and in failed payments.

Financial fraud in the eyes of the banks is when we have proof that the card was reported by the issuer (the bank) that a transaction was not authorized by the owner of the bank card, this event creates a chargeback. Authorities are willing to investigate this type of fraud since it can involve stolen cards, data leaks from banks etc.

A failed payment is when the card does not have enough funds to cover the cost of the trip.
This happens more often than not, several good clients do not have the money to pay us but later we manage to get the money via retries of the capture event.  Remember, with a ride hailing it is easy to go higher than the pre-authorization amount and hence create a bigger capture amount. Banks normally do not consider this as a financial fraud but rather a bad debt management from our part.
We “technically speaking” can still get the money of those fraudulent drivers, but these drivers are able to abuse the system by triggering a high fail payment that is very unlikely to be recovered. 
These drivers are confirmed to be abusing our system, but since the clients are still owing us money we are afraid that in the eyes of the authorities this type of loss is not considered proper financial fraud.



We would rather not report these drivers because of 2 main issues.
A) we will have to explain that we detect those drivers by linking them by the same creation of the IP of the users and therefore we will be exposing how our system works. 
B) it takes a lot of time from fraud operations to put the case together per driver, we rather spent that time reducing fraud losses elsewhere.

Hi Helen

as individual’s image falls into scope of ‘personal data’ definition, we need to ensure that we can demonstrate appropriate legal grounds to record and further process it.

For non-paid partnerships, this will require consent from the data subjects (i.e. both drivers and riders). This has to be collected prior to the recording, which means that the camera shouldn’t be turned on by default and the recording should only start after the consent is properly obtained (verbal consent would be insufficient here, especially if the plan is to further distribute one’s image). For consent to be valid, it has to be given freely and there shouldn’t be any negative consequences if our employee or a rider chooses not to be recorded. The consent should be also accompanied with privacy notice including standard disclosures around our processing activities. 

Please note that under GDPR consent can be revoked at any time - so there might be a risk that once the video is up, our driver or a rider withdraws the consent and - from legal perspective - it would be recommended to take the video down or to make appropriate changes to the material so it would no longer include an image of respective driver/rider.

Please let me know if this legal set up makes sense for you business-wise. If so - I’ll draft necessary consent and privacy notice.

Best,

Adriana

[https://www.freshworks.com/crm/customer-journey-mapping/?tactic_id=4305683&utm_source=Google-Adwords&utm_campaign=Fsales-Search-DSA%2BRLSAInside-E-EU&utm_term=&device=c&utm_medium=Fsales-Search-DSA%2BRLSAInside-E-EU&gclid=Cj0KCQiA0eOPBhCGARIsAFIwTs6BrCEqVR8W2GJUYb5AhEqyPi-aZyjaSNOWIxJq8KljpnsN7eVyNAEaAgnZEALw_wcB|https://www.freshworks.com/crm/customer-journey-mapping/?tactic_id=4305683&utm_source=Google-Adwords&utm_campaign=Fsales-Search-DSA%2BRLSAInside-E-EU&utm_term=&device=c&utm_medium=Fsales-Search-DSA%2BRLSAInside-E-EU&gclid=Cj0KCQiA0eOPBhCGARIsAFIwTs6BrCEqVR8W2GJUYb5AhEqyPi-aZyjaSNOWIxJq8KljpnsN7eVyNAEaAgnZEALw_wcB|smart-link] (the examples given there are more about purchasing some items/services)

{quote}*Creating a customer journey map*

Customer Journey Mapping has two main aspects - storytelling and visualization. To create this powerful tool, follow the steps listed below:

* Gather qualitative and quantitative data on audience

* Use the data to build an audience persona and set clear objectives

* Identify all the touchpoints

* Analyze the different phases of the customer journey

* Take the customer journey yourself

* Optimize your customer journey map{quote}

[https://uxdesign.cc/how-to-use-journey-mapping-for-your-project-10282a79182a|https://uxdesign.cc/how-to-use-journey-mapping-for-your-project-10282a79182a|smart-link] ⭐ 

{quote}There are two types of journey maps: *actual and planned*. Actual journey maps are retrospective and map out how users currently interact with a product or service. Planned journey maps are prospective and map out how you expect or would like users to interact with a product or service.{quote}

{quote}At its essence, a journey map is a table with stages through time on the horizontal axis and themes for analysis on the vertical axis. The steps on the horizontal axis vary according to the topic of your analysis; The vertical axis usually consists of similar themes like touch points, pain points, emotions, thoughts, and opportunities.{quote}

|| ||*Stage 1*||*Stage 2*||*Stage 3*||
|Touch points| | | |
|Pain points| | | |
|Emotions| | | |
|Barriers ?| | | |
|Thoughts| | | |
|Information needed| | | |
|Opportunities| | | |

{quote}Several data collection methods can be used and different types of data are combined and triangulated. Examples of methods include diary studies, interviews, web analytics, social media listening, and surveys.{quote}

{quote}Journey mapping is a flexible tool, there are many ways of how to use it. The main goal is to communicate the users’ experiences with a product or service. Based on the goal of your project you may choose to emphasize or leave out certain parts.{quote}

[https://www.nngroup.com/articles/customer-journey-mapping/|https://www.nngroup.com/articles/customer-journey-mapping/|smart-link] 

{quote}While journey maps vary based on the specific context for which they are used, they tend to follow a general model that includes zones for the “lens,” the mapped experience, and the insights learned throughout the process.{quote}

!image-20220201-125155.png|width=998,height=684!

{quote}*Shift a company’s perspective from inside-out to outside-in.* If an organization lets internal processes and systems drive decisions that affect customer experience, a journey map could help turn the culture of that organization by refocusing on the thoughts, actions and emotions of customers. Journey mapping sheds light on real human experiences that often organizations know very little about.{quote}

{quote}*Key Elements of Customer Journey Maps*

While journey maps can (and should) take a wide variety of forms, certain elements are generally included:

*Point of view.* <…> “Actors” usually aligns with personas, if they exist. As a guideline, when creating a basic journey map, use one point of view per map in order to provide a strong, clear narrative.

*Scenario.* Next, determine the specific experience to map. <…> Make sure to clarify the user’s goal during this experience.

*Actions, mindsets, and emotions.* At the heart of a journey map’s narrative is what the user is doing, thinking, and feeling during the journey. These data points should be based on qualitative research, such as field studies, contextual inquiry, and diary studies.

*Touchpoints and channels.* The map should align touchpoints (times when the actor in the map actually interacts with the company) and channels (methods of communication or service delivery, such as the website or physical store) with user goals and actions. These elements deserve a special emphasis because they are often where brand inconsistencies and disconnected experiences are uncovered.

*Insights and ownership.* The entire point of the journey-mapping process is to uncover gaps in the user experience (which are particularly common in omnichannel journeys), and then take action to optimize the experience.{quote}

{quote}To make informed decisions on those tradeoffs, consider the following:

* What level of detail is needed in order to tell the complete story?

* What elements (such as device, channel, encountered content) are also necessary in order to provide the most truthful narrative?

* Is the purpose of this journey map to diagnose issues with a current experience or to design a new experience?

* What’s the balance between external actions (on the customer side) and internal actions (on the organization side)?

* Who will be using this journey map?{quote}

{quote}*Rules for Creating Successful Journey Maps*

*Establish the “why" and the “what.”* First, identify the business goal that the journey map will support. Make sure there are clear answers to these basic key questions before you begin the process:

* What business goal does this journey map support?

* Who will use it?

* Who is it about and what experience does it address?

* How will it be shared?

*Base it on truth.* Journey maps should result in truthful narratives, not fairy tales. Start with gathering any existing research, but additional journey-based research is also needed to fill in the gaps that the existing research won’t cover. This is a qualitative-research process. While quantitative data can help support or validate (or aid in convincing stakeholders who may view qualitative data as “fuzzy”), quantitative data alone cannot build a story.

*Collaborate with others.* <…> Pull back the curtain and invite stakeholders from various groups to be a part of compiling the data and building the map.

*Don’t jump to visualization.* <…> Make sure the synthesis of your data is complete and well-understood before moving to creating the visual.

*Engage others with the end product.* Don’t expect to get “buy-in” and foster interest in your journey map by simply sending a lovely graphic as an email attachment. Make it a living interactive document that people can be a part of. Bring up your story in meetings and conversations to promote a narrative that others believe in and begin to reference. One idea is to create a journey-mapping showroom where anyone not on the direct team can come experience the process and resulting artefacts.{quote}

The template - [https://media.nngroup.com/media/articles/attachments/JMTemplate.pdf|https://media.nngroup.com/media/articles/attachments/JMTemplate.pdf]

[https://www.nngroup.com/articles/journey-mapping-101/|https://www.nngroup.com/articles/journey-mapping-101/|smart-link] ⭐ 

{quote}*Key Components of a Journey Map*

Journey maps come in all shapes and sizes. Regardless of how they look, journey maps have the following 5 key elements in common:

1. Actor

2. Scenario + Expectations

Journey maps are best for scenarios that involve a sequence of events (such as shopping or taking a trip), describe a process (thus involve a set of transitions over time), or might involve multiple +channels+.

3. Journey Phases

Journey phases are the different high-level stages in the journey. They provide organization for the rest of the information in the journey map (actions, thoughts, and emotions). 

4. Actions, Mindsets, and Emotions

These are behaviors, thoughts, and feelings the actor has throughout the journey and that are mapped within each of the journey phases.

*Actions* are the actual behaviors and steps taken by users. This component is not meant to be a granular step-by-step log of every discrete interaction. Rather, it is a narrative of the steps the actor takes during that phase.

*Mindsets* correspond to users’ thoughts, questions, motivations, and information needs at different stages in the journey. Ideally, these are customer verbatims from research.

*Emotions* are plotted as single line across the journey phases, literally signaling the emotional “ups” and “downs” of the experience. Think of this line as a contextual layer of emotion that tells us where the user is delighted versus frustrated.

5. Opportunities

Opportunities (along with additional context such as ownership and metrics) are insights gained from mapping; they speak to how the user experience can be optimized. Insights and opportunities help the team draw knowledge from the map:

* What needs to be done with this knowledge?

* Who owns what change?

* Where are the biggest opportunities?

* How are we going to measure improvements we implement?{quote}

{quote}*Journey-Map Variations*

* User experience maps - agnostic of a specific business or product. It’s used for understanding a general human behavior; in contrast, a customer journey map is specific and focused on a particular business or product.

* Service blueprints visualize the relationships between different service components (such as people or processes) at various touchpoints in a specific customer journey. <…> They are extensions of journey maps, but instead of being focused on the user (and taking the user’s viewpoint), they are focused on the business (and take its perspective).
* User story maps are for planning and implementation (think little picture).{quote}

[https://www.nngroup.com/articles/customer-journey-mapping-process/|https://www.nngroup.com/articles/customer-journey-mapping-process/|smart-link] 

!image-20220201-134806.png|width=803,height=514!

[https://www.nngroup.com/articles/service-blueprints-definition/|https://www.nngroup.com/articles/service-blueprints-definition/|smart-link] ⭐ 

{quote}A service blueprint corresponds to a specific customer journey and the specific user goals associated to that journey. This journey can vary in scope. Thus, for the same service, you may have multiple blueprints if there are several different scenarios that it can accommodate. For example, with a restaurant business, you may have separate service blueprints for the tasks of ordering food for takeout versus dining in the restaurant.

Service blueprints should always align to a business goal: reducing redundancies, improving the employee experience, or converging siloed processes.{quote}

{quote}Blueprints are treasure maps that help businesses *discover weaknesses*. Poor user experiences are often due to an internal organizational shortcoming — a weak link in the ecosystem. While we can quickly understand what may be wrong in a user interface (bad design or a broken button), determining the root cause of a systemic issue (such as corrupted data or long wait times) is much more difficult. Blueprinting exposes the big picture and offers a map of dependencies, thus allowing a business to discover a weak leak at its roots.

<…> blueprints help *identify opportunities for optimization*. The visualization of relationships in blueprints uncovers potential improvements and ways to eliminate redundancy. <…>

Blueprinting is most useful when coordinating complex services because it *bridges crossdepartment efforts*.{quote}

!image-20220201-144230.png|width=1126,height=1198!

{quote}*Key Elements of a Service Blueprint*

*Customer actions*

Steps, choices, activities, and interactions that customer performs while interacting with a service to reach a particular goal. Customer actions are derived from research or a customer-journey map.

*Frontstage actions*

Actions that occur directly in view of the customer. These actions can be human-to-human or human-to-computer actions. Human-to-human actions are the steps and activities that the contact employee (the person who interacts with the customer) performs. Human-to-computer actions are carried out when the customer interacts with self-service technology (for example, a mobile app or an ATM).

_<…>_

_Note that there is not always a parallel frontstage action for every customer touchpoint. A customer can interact directly with a service without encountering a frontstage actor <…>. Each time a customer interacts with a service (through an employee or via technology), a_ *_moment of truth_* _occurs. During these moments of truth, customers judge your quality and make decisions regarding future purchases._

*Backstage actions*

Steps and activities that occur behind the scenes to support onstage happenings. These actions could be performed by a backstage employee (e.g., a cook in the kitchen) or by a frontstage employee who does something not visible to the customer (e.g., a waiter entering an order into the kitchen display system).

_​_*Processes*

Internal steps, and interactions that support the employees in delivering the service.

_This element includes anything that must occur for all of the above to take place. Processes for the appliance company include credit-card verification, pricing, delivery of units to the store from the factory, writing quality tests, and so on._

The last layer of a service blueprint is evidence, which is made of the props and places that anyone in the blueprint has an exchange with. Evidence can be involved in both frontstage and backstage processes and actions.{quote}

!image-20220201-145245.png|width=908,height=1143!

{quote}*Secondary Elements to Include in a Service Blueprint*

Blueprints can be adapted to context and business goals by introducing the additional elements as needed: 

*Arrows* 

Arrows are a key element of service blueprinting. They indicate relationships, and more importantly, dependencies. A single arrow suggests a linear, one-way exchange, while a double arrow suggests the need for agreement and codependency.

*Time*

If time is a primary variable in your service, an estimated duration for each customer action should be represented in your blueprint.

*Regulations or Policy*

Any given policies or regulations that dictate how a process is completed (food regulations, security policies, etc.) can be added to your blueprint. This information will allow us to understand what can and cannot be changed as we optimize.

*Emotion*

Similar to how a user’s emotion is represented throughout a customer-journey map, employees’ emotions can be represented in the blueprint. (Emotion is shown through the green and red faces in the example below.) Where are employees frustrated? Where are employees happy and motivated? If you already have some qualitative data regarding points of frustration (possibly obtained from internal surveys or other methods), you can use them in the blueprint to help focus the design process and more easily locate pain points.

*Metrics*

Any success metric that can provide context to your blueprint is a benefit, especially if buy-in is the blueprint’s goal. An example may be the time spent on various processes, or the financial costs associated with them. These numbers will help the business identify where time or money are wasted due to miscommunication or other inefficiencies.{quote}

{quote}Service blueprints are companions to customer-journey maps: they help organizations see the big picture of how a service is implemented by the company and used by the customers. They pinpoint dependencies between employee-facing and customer-facing processes in the same visualization and are instrumental in identifying pain points, optimizing complex interactions, and ultimately saving money for the organization and improving the experience for its customers.{quote}

Hi Alina, please see complete set of answers below. Please let me know in case of any further questions.


* _Is our understanding correct that if any of our stores exceed the area of 300 square meters, we are obliged to conclude an agreement with the deposit system operator for each store?_

Bolt (or any other store owner) would have to conclude an agreement with the deposit system operator for each store whose +sales area+ is:

* 300 m^2^ or more - if the store is located in a municipality with the status of “state city” (i.e., the cities of Daugavpils, Jelgava, Jēkabpils, Jūrmala, Liepāja, Ogre, Rēzekne, Rīga, Valmiera and Ventspils).
* 60 m^2^ or more - if the store is located in any other municipality.

“Sales area” means the physical space which is available to buyers for browsing the store and making purchases. If the store performs only distance sales, then it would not have any “sales area” within the meaning of law and accordingly the store owner would not have to participate in the deposit-return system. Even if the buyers can come and pick up the orders, this is still considered distance sale. However, if the buyers can choose the products on-site, then it would likely qualify as a “sales area” within the meaning of law.

* _Is our understanding correct that if our store does not exceed the area of 300 square meters, each store has to place the information on the nearest address and opening hours of the place of acceptance of the deposit packaging? Are our stores obliged to use the template reflected here in order to inform the clients_ [_DP tirgotaju posters A3 (depozitapunkts.lv)_|https://depozitapunkts.lv/uploads/catalogue-product-files30/files/DP-tirgotaju-posters-A3-editable-v2.pdf]_?_

You are right, if your store does not have an obligation to participate in the deposit-return system, then you must place this information in or near the store (please note the previous answer, the threshold for participation is 300 m^2^ only in state cities, in the majority of municipalities the threshold is only 60 m^2^). However, this obligation applies only to stores tat perform physical sales on-site. If the sales are performed only through distance means, then no such information needs to be displayed.

No, the linked template is not mandatory, it is only an example for convenience.

* _Is our understanding correct that our stores shall calculate once a year how many reusable packaging of beverages have not been returned and make adjustments to the annual VAT return?_

No, stores (that only sell beverages in deposit packaging) do not have an obligation to adjust the annual VAT return. This obligation lies only on the producer, because the seller at first sells beverages (and applies VAT also to the packaging) but later receives back some of the empty packaging. For this reason the producer calculates the unreturned reusable packaging, submits an annual VAT return and adjusts the taxable value of the delivered goods for the value of that packaging, which it has not received within the year.

Вопрос:
Считается ли Людмила Г. имеющей судимость согласно законодательству Украины?

*Сколько по времени лицо считается имеющим судимость?*
Согласно ст. 88 Криминального Кодекса Украины "лицо признается имеющим судимость со дня вступления в законную силу обвинительного приговора и _до погашения или снятия судимости_".
Это значит, что с того момента, как судимость снята или погашена, по общему правилу лицо считается не имеющим судимости, и на него не распространяются связанные с судимостью ограничения. Считается, что уголовное право исходит из принципов гуманизма, и человек, который отбыл наказание, не должен вечно стигматизироваться обществом.
Людмила совершила преступление по ч.2 ст. 286 ККУ, которое предусматривает до 8 лет лишения свободы (то есть это тяжкое преступление), и, согласно имеющемуся у нас в распоряжении решению суда, она была приговорена к 3 годам лишения свободы.
Порядок погашения/снятия судимости предусмотрен в ст. 89, 90 ККУ (по общему правилу за тяжкие преступления - 6 лет после отбытия наказания), и зависит от ряда обстоятельств, которые нам сейчас не известны - когда Людмила закончила отбывать наказание, была ли Людмила освобождена от отбывания наказания в связи с беременностью, освободили ли ее по УДО, совершала ли она новые преступления и тд.

*Имеет ли Людмила судимость в настоящее время?*
Чтобы точно узнать, имеет ли Людмила судимость в настоящее время, нужно запросить у нее справку о привлечении к уголовной ответственности, отсутствии (наличии) судимости или ограничений, предусмотренных уголовным процессуальным законодательством Украины.
Сразу обращу внимание на то, что МВД Украины выдает 2 вида справок - "сокращенную" и "полную". Отличие в том, что первая только указывает, имеется ли судимость на момент запроса (такая справка не включает снятые/погашенные судимости), а вторая включает все случаи привлечения к отвественности, даже если судимость была погашена. Для целей наших [T&Cs для водителей|https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/legal/ua/terms-for-drivers/] достаточно "сокращенной" справки, однако если будет какое-либо обсуждение в прессе, нам лучше иметь полную справку для понимания контекста и готовности дать комментарии.
Вполне вероятно, что судимость Людмилы уже могла быть снята или погашена, и в таком случае юридически она считается не имеющей судимости. С погашенной/снятой судимостью по ее статье она вполне могла бы работать даже полицейским/гражданским служащим, поэтому я не вижу причин, по которым мы должны исключить ее из розыгрыша, если ее судимость погашена / снята.Также обращу внимание на то, что для запроса у Людмилы справки о несудимости по-хорошему нужно проверить, что она давала нам согласие на обработку персональных данных.

[@anni.faltis|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U8PJ6RL7P] and I discussed the proposed solution for using a very long-term scheduled block or removing the driving licence instead of hard-blocking a user.

*To re-cap:*

* These alternative solutions (long-term scheduled block and removing the DL) were proposed _as a temporary solution while we’re waiting for a permanent functionality_ to hard-block a user per product vertical or user type (depending on the particular event and Admin functionality).
* Scheduled block and removing the DL allows us to get revenue from users who we don’t want to be using Drive but who could still use other Bolt services

As shared by [@anni.faltis|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U8PJ6RL7P] , these are the *issues with the proposed alternative solutions*:

* There are plans for implementing this same alternative solution for all product verticals - therefore this temporary process change will eventually become obsolete
* Using a scheduled block requires adding an end date for the block, which opens room for manual errors
* If the agents start using the 7-year block, we’d need to go over these user profiles in 7 years to ensure they are still blocked

With this being discussed, the Safety team is aware of our needs for custom blocking options for the different events we encounter. Additionally, the Safety CS TLs and STLs are currently working on a project and mapping what kind of blocking logic is required for handling high priority events. Therefore Safety team suggests that we *hold off on this separate process for Drive for now* - and wait for more directions from the Safety team. This means, however, that we would prevent such users from using any Bolt services by hard-blocking them. 

----

(1) As mentioned the new contract (as with the old one) has an automatic renewal date. This is fine as long as we diarise to serve notice in good time if we decide to move on next year to a different office.

(2) Payment of invoices are in advance and within 14 days of presentation of invoice.
