(3) The limitation of liability under the contract is limited to premeditated or gross negligence and contractual damages available for the breach of the contract. This is generally acceptable as any personal injury of death caused within the building is excluded but we should as for a copy of their insurance policy or get confirmation that any injuries within the building will be covered by the landlord.

(4) Our competitors are permitted to be in the same building so please ensure that out part of the building is either locked from other occupants in the building or we have adequate security measures in place to prevent people from seeing our company information. {code:sql}with rh_searches as (
select * from (
select search_categories_overview__session_id as session_id,
search_categories_overview__user_id as user_id,
search_categories_overview__created as created,
search_categories_overview__lat as lat,
search_categories_overview__lng as lng,
row_number() over (partition by search_categories_overview__session_id order by search_categories_overview__created asc) search_in_session
from etl_search_denormalized_view esdv 
where search_categories_overview__city_id=1
and search_categories_overview__created between '2022-01-17' and '2022-01-31'
)
where search_in_session=1
),
drive_verified_users as (
select distinct user_id, 
last_value(status) over (partition by user_id order by created asc rows between unbounded preceding and unbounded following) verification_state
from carsharing.rental_user_user_verification_state ruuvs 
),
drive_availability as (
select * from 
(
select 
vehicle_id,
lag(created,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc) prev_created,
created,
value_old as from_state,
value_new as to_state,
lat,
lng
from carsharing.rental_car_order_vehicle_state_event rcovse 
where created>'2022-01-01' and type='state'
)
where from_state = 'waiting_for_order'
order by vehicle_id asc,created asc
) 
select 
	count(session_id) search_sessions,
	count(case when verification_state in ('verified','verified_manually') then session_id else null end) search_sessions_from_verified_users,
	count(case when verification_state in ('verified','verified_manually') and carsharing_availability>0 then session_id else null end) search_sessions_from_verified_users_with_cars_nearby
from (
select 
	rhs.*,
	dvu.verification_state,
	count(distinct da.vehicle_id) carsharing_availability
from rh_searches rhs
left join drive_verified_users dvu on rhs.user_id=dvu.user_id
left join drive_availability da
	on rhs.created > da.prev_created and rhs.created < da.created
	and ST_DistanceSphere(ST_POINT(rhs.lng,rhs.lat),ST_POINT(da.lng,da.lat))<200
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6,7
){code}

Hi Henelin, 

As discussed via slack, general procedure for moving an employee from one company to another requires terminating the employment contract and entering into new one with the new employer, because Bolt Operations and Bolt Technology are separate legal entities. For the employee this means interruption of the length of service which affects some of social guarantees provided by employment laws. Taking into account that this is intra-group movement where employee is being promoted it is possible to transfer the employment contract unamended to another Bolt entity by an agreement between all three parties. In such case the length of service wont be interrupted. From legal side this means that the new employer replaces the old one by taking over all rights and obligation arising from the employment relationship. 

Important to note. Bolt Options are always granted by Bolt Technology, even if the employee is employed by Bolt Operations. If the employee is transferred from Bolt Technology to Bolt Operations then Bolt Options Agreement remains in Bolt Technology (this will not be transferred).

h1. Certificate Statuses

EJBCA manages the statuses of certificates in the database using integer value. For reference, these are described here:

|Value|Numerical Value|Description|
|CERT_UNASSIGNED|0|Certificate doesn't belong to anyone. Not used much anymore in EJBCA|
|CERT_INACTIVE|10|Assigned, but not yet active Not used much anymore in EJBCA|
|CERT_ROLLOVERPENDING|11|Certificate is a new CA certificate which will become valid in the future.|
|CERT_ACTIVE|20|Certificate is active and assigned.|
|CERT_NOTIFIEDABOUTEXPIRATION|21|Certificate is still active and the user is notified that it will soon expire.|
|CERT_REVOKED|40|Certificate is revoked, permanently or temporarily.|
|CERT_ARCHIVED|60|Certificate is expired and kept for archive purpose. Gets set automatically when a certificate is included in CRL.|

Proposal: 
change the structure from one buffer to two buffers, one for track/event and one for identify.
having one buffer for all might be a source of a problem in the following situation:

lets consider a big batch of identify/sync calls:
events and identifies are queued together to the same buffer,
but there are 10x more events than identify calls so they always take the most of the buffer while big batch of identify calls get only part of it,
before sync will finish “flush” will be executed several times extending the time needed for /identify/sync/bulk endpoint to finish.

This is not a big problem in case of  simple version of /identify/sync endpoint (not bulk).
For this our own lib could introduce immediate sending pattern without buffering.

Hey there Nisley,

*About cancellation fee thresholds:*
As you may know, the cancellation fee setup usually varies by market, or even by city/category. 
What’s happening here is that the same self-help article (EN version) is shared by multiple markets, therefore the range must accommodate a wide variety of setups. The market-specific information is currently available only in the PT version of the article. Self-help is not the best place to keep this information as the info can change often and is accessible to riders in-app anyway, in real-time. Therefore, we will most likely remove the mention of specific thresholds and ranges from self-help in the future. 💭 

*About cancellation fee amounts:*
We want to avoid keeping pricing in the KB as the information is subject to change and is always up to date and accessible to CS in Admin, instructions for checking the information are included in the following articles:

* [🔒 Driver reports cancellation fee or wait time fee was not charged|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013304500--Driver-reports-cancellation-fee-or-wait-time-fee-was-not-charged]
* [🔒 Rider reports they were charged cancellation fee|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360012407420--Rider-reports-they-were-charged-cancellation-fee]

Therefore, we would propose removing the pricing info (rates + cancellation and wait fees) from KB altogether: [🇵🇹 Categories and Rates|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360011487333--Categories-and-Rates]

Hi [~accountid:60630d4b8a0f7c006fb3738d] - in short, the best approach would be to ask concerned drivers to call back using a number readily available on Bolt’s website. That way they would have confidence that they are speaking to a Bolt representative. For what it’s worth, this is how I personally deal with any ‘cold call’ because, as our drivers are conscious of, there really is no real way of knowing the legitimacy of any ‘cold call’. Bolt could also potentially send a message to a driver in the App asking them to get in touch.

What Bolt should +*not*+ do is give out any personal information for a driver (i.e. “Hi, Bolt here, we can prove we’re Bolt because your contact details are X and your earnings are Y”), at least not until the driver has confirmed his own identity. Even if such information is not protected personal information, if would nevertheless be extremely embarrassing for Bolt to disclose any information about a driver to anyone that _isn’t_ that driver. 

The alternative approach is to relay limited obtuse and non-personal information concerning the drivers activities, such as the final four digits of a driver’s two most recent invoices numbers or similarly obtuse yet specific information (but absolutely +*no personal details*+ until a driver has verified his own identity). Of course, this might not always satisfy a driver and they might not be able to check such information on the spot.

In summary, asking a driver to call Bolt back is probably the best option. 

Thanks.

Hi [~accountid:61027984a539cb006846c64f]\! The short answer is no, we can’t sell electronic cigarettes in our Bolt Market stores in Latvia. Please see the relevant laws and explanations below.

----

Article 8(2) of the Law [On the Handling of Tobacco Products, Herbal Products for Smoking, Electronic Smoking Devices and Their Liquids|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/282077-on-the-handling-of-tobacco-products-herbal-products-for-smoking-electronic-smoking-devices-and-their-liquids] (the Law) states that:

_“Tobacco products, electronic smoking devices, and refill containers may not be sold and purchased using a distance contract, including outside the territory of a European Union Member State or a state of the European Economic Area.”_

 

Article 14(8) of the Law states that:

_“For the sale and purchase of tobacco products, electronic smoking devices, or their refill containers using a distance contract, a fine from twenty to forty-two units of fine shall be imposed on a natural person but a fine from forty to one hundred and forty units of fine - on a legal person.”_ (a unit of fine is EUR 5)

 

In the market there always have been some market participants that do not comply with the above regulation either because they are not aware of it or simply ignore it.



However, although not electronic cigarettes, currently such devices as IQOS (tobacco heating devices) and other products such as tobacco free nicotine pouches are not regulated under the Law, thus currently they do not fall under the ban. However, the draft amendments to the Law are already being reviewed by the Latvian parliament and once approved they shall also fall under the distance sale ban.

PCO badge and Private Hire Driver License (PHL) are two different documents, with different purposes. The event categories are naturally under Driver Operating In Fraudulent Manner grouping, so changing this process from asking the PHL document to asking PCO badge instead, would make it easier for the driver.

Their offer for drivers is not mature yet so at this stage, I would recommend to keep this low case and reassess the situation once we’ve experienced it with a few drivers.

The contract requires us to:

* make our best efforts to allow up to 30 drivers to join JUMP DRIVER to carry out their transport services through Jump
* communicate some content / documents provided by Jump to the drivers  
* communicate to Jump the contact details of the Targeted Drivers 
* communicate to Jump the information necessary to establish the drivers' payslips 
* obtain regular feedback from the drivers on their views regarding the status of ‘contractor-employee’ and forward that feedback to Jump, etc.

→ This contract raises Privacy questions (in particular we would need to obtain the driver’s consent to transmit their details to Jump) and could also give the impression that we overstep our role - which, as a platform, should be limited to supporting Bolt OU activities, drivers training, drivers and passengers assistance. In my opinion, we shouldn’t have a role of intermediary between drivers and ‘employers' or ‘contracting agencies’.

I would perhaps instead recommend that we (unformally) promote Jump services to some of our drivers who we think would be interested. If we think this attracts a number of people, we could also envisage if we could promote this on our Bolt Marketplace.

Happy to discuss further though if this is something that you think would definitely help our business or a partnership that you think is worth developing for our activities.

*PROBLEM STATEMENTS*

* 50% of Drive KB articles and 55 sub-processes in total contain instructions for escalations to the #transcom-bolt_carsharing_ee channel

* Duplicate information:
** agents posting the same details both on Admin and Slack
** agents' Slack reports contain details or images that are readily available in Admin 
* Clutter in Slack reports causing difficulties for OPS to prioritise tasks
* Difficult to establish correct priority and handling time expectations CS agents
* Reporting limitations for Slack escalations



*GOALS*

*Scalability* - escalation practices that are scalable across different Drive markets

*Better prioritisation -* workflow for OPS to prioritise and handle reported issues efficiently

*Easy to understand processes -* escalation processes for CS that are easy to understand and set correct expectations

*Reduced effort on all fronts -* free up resources for more important process changes by reducing unnecessary work for Content

*Reduce CS costs* due to simpler processes and less time spent escalating the issues


*SOLUTION*

Move from single-channel (Slack) —> multiple channels with different priorities:

# *OPS Service Desk*: low priority tasks with no need for CS follow-ups
# *Zendesk:* Alleviate OPS workload by having Tier-2 CS, Escalation Specialist, Case Manager handle certain escalations (can escalate further to OPS if needed)
# *Admin*: utilising existing functionalities and building new ones
# *Slack*: reserved only for high priority, high urgency tasks that require active communication between CS<>OPS

* Changes we can already start with (no limitations)

* Discuss specific processes highlighted by Henriko


*MEETING OUTCOMES:*

* A clear vision of OPS workflows in Admin
* Action items for the escalation improvement action plan

+*UPDATE RE APPROACH FOR RIDE HAILING LAUNCH IN BELGIUM - JAN 2022*+

+A+ +*new temporary regime*+ +was adopted in Brussels just before Christmas. That brought a number of changes in the approach for our ride-hailing operations launch in Brussels (ETA adjusted to 1st Feb)+:

* The temporary solution will only benefit LVC drivers who obtained their license prior to 15 Jan 2021. So LVC drivers who obtained their license after 15 Jan 2021 would still be subject to the 1995 Regulation.
* *Riders Association (RA) no longer needed*, at least not in order to try to comply with the 1995 Regulation.
* Business decision not to keep the RA just for the benefit of the LVC drivers mentioned above (who obtained their license prior to 15 Jan 2021).
* Outside counsel confirmed that the RA would not offer any administrative advantages for Bolt. Therefore it exists but we won’t use it.
* Decision was taken to launch on the basis of the temporary regime and then switch to compliance with the Pan Taxi when it comes into force.

+The new Temporary Regime sets out 3 requirements+:

* Have an *establishment unit* in Belgium registered in the Belgian company register \[_avoir, en Belgique, une unité d’établissement enregistrée à la Banque-Carrefour des Entreprises_]
* Make an *electronic taxi reservation service* available to the public \[_mettre à la disposition du public un service de réservation électronique de services de taxis_]
* *Allow the administration to access electronically the following information, which must be permanently updated*: driver/operator T&Cs, which must not restrict affiliation to other platforms or foresee increased costs in that case,  customer T&Cs, identification data of registered drivers and operators \[_permettre à la direction Transport de Personnes de Bruxelles Mobilité d’accéder électroniquement aux informations suivantes, mises à jour en permanence : a) les données d’identification des exploitants et des chauffeurs enregistrés sur la plateforme ;) les conditions générales d’affiliation à la plateforme applicables aux exploitants et aux chauffeurs, lesquelles ne peuvent ni leur interdire de s’affilier également à d’autres plateformes de leur choix, ni imposer de surcoût à ceux qui s’affilient à plusieurs plateformes ; c) les conditions générales d’utilisation de la plateforme applicables aux clients_]

* Outside Counsel recommended to *set up an Establishment Unit*, as required by the new temporary regime.
* Please see separate ticket for this:[ LEGAL-7209: BELGIUM - Corporate formalities for RH launch|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LEGAL-7209][*PENDING*|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LEGAL-7209]

* No license currently required for Brussels Taxis.
* License for Flanders 'taxis' already obtained.

[^Bolt Car Program risk analysis 28 January 2022 VF(1436478.1) (1).pdf]

+Summary+: 

* The Bolt Car Project *increases the risks of a driver benefiting from such offer being reclassified as an employee* (rather than an independent contractor), as a driver could argue in front of a judge that Bolt is incentivising him to drive mainly through the Bolt app in order to get a reduced rent for his car. This increased risk is due to the combination of Additional Earning + Bolt car sticker (see below for details).
* OC assess that the Bolt Car project could *increase Bolt’s risks related to reclassification about 20%*. This assessment is based on the fact that the Bolt Car project includes additional ‘clues’ (i.e., branding, Additional Earnings, etc.) of reclassification of the business relationship as an employment relationship.
* _To better understand, French Courts have established a bundle of ‘clues’ (faisceau d'indices) to determine if there is a_ +_subordination link_+ _between the platforms and their drivers during the connections to the platforms. Examples of indicators likely to characterize a subordination link and therefore an employment relationship:_ 
** _the fact that the drivers do not freely set their prices;_ 
** _the fact that the drivers must wear clothing identifying the platform's name;_
** _the power to sanction drivers (directly and/or indirectly) when they do not met some requirements imposed by the platform;_ 
** _the fact that drivers cannot build up their own clientele or provide services to several customers / exclusivity towards employer._
* *‘Additional Earnings’*: From a French employment law, the ‘Additional Earnings’ from the Bolt Car Project could be considered as a ‘clue’ for the judges to characterize an employment relationship, considering that:
** The amount of the Additional Earnings would be unilaterally set by Bolt and not freely set by the driver;
** By granting such bonus to some drivers and not to others, Bolt would indirectly penalize the drivers who do not complete a minimum of 30 rides per week through the Bolt app;
** The Additional Earnings could be compared to an incentive plans implemented for employees to encourage them to work more and obtain better results;
** Bolt could be considered by judges as being the exclusive employer of drivers, preventing them from working with others platforms. 
* *Bolt stickers on cars*: 
** The fact that the drivers have to drive the cars leased with Bolt stickers could also constitute a clue of the subordination link → Such branding could be considered as a way for Bolt to indirectly constraint drivers to work exclusively for Bolt.
** French law also prohibits agreements and practices that have as effect to substantially restrict the possibility for a VTC service to promote, via external signs on the vehicle, one or more transport offers.
* *Contract term*: The fact that the contract would be limited to 6 months would not reduce the risks related to a potential reclassification, as a Labour Court could consider that the employment relationship has been characterized during this time period. Though it is true that the longest the lease will be, the highest the risk would be from a practical standpoint.
* *Mitigation measures*: OC recommended a few mitigation measures (which would only reduce the reclassification risks, not eliminate them):
** ensuring / reiterating the +possibility for drivers to rent cars from others leasing companies+; and
** removing the obligation to lease cars with Bolt stickers - e.g. consider indicating in the contract that +drivers are free to+ 1. remove the Bolt sticker or at least 2. +add any other promotional signs on the rented vehicle+ + avoiding that the Bolt sticker is present on all the car surface.
* *Tripartite agreement between the driver, Bolt and Clicar*:
** It is possible under French law for a party to be authorized to pay, on behalf of
another party, a sum that the latest owes to a third party.
** However each parties’ role should be clarified and +OC recommends to avoid having La Maison du Chauffeur VTC (++_La Maison_++) as a party to the contract+.
** La Maison’s intermediary role would not reduce reclassification risks for Bolt (as drivers provide services only to Bolt).
** OC recommends that La Maison should just provides services to Bolt which it invoices separately.
** It is however possible to envisage subcontracting some tasks to La Maison, such as the information presentation and provision re the number of rides and the sums obtained. But then Bolt must ensure 1. that drivers have been informed that some of their personal data are transferred to La Maison and 2. that La Maison presents sufficient guarantees in terms of confidentiality and data security + a Data Processing Agreement must be signed. *→* [~accountid:611bc3aeaee32f006f907fbc] [~accountid:5ccc2af0cf9b780e6a3a5139] *Please confirm La Maison’s role* 😉 
* *Advertisement*: We could envisage an ads along those lines:

« _Louez une voiture à partir de \[205] Euros par semaine grâce à l’offre Bolt < > Clicar - Faites un minimum de 31 courses par semaine avec Bolt et Bolt paie une partie de votre loyer à Clicar_ ».

Hi\!

As discussed, consent would be the most safe and conservative approach. Also not likely to be challenged by the regulator.

# *Recordkeeping* of the consent. We should be able to demonstrate that the data subject has given consent to the processing activity.
This means that we need to keep the records of such consents given. We should keep this evidence for +as long as we are still processing based on the consent+. So at least as long as we are providing the data to the fleets based on this consent, we should keep the record of consent given. 

# *Withdrawal of consent.* The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time. The withdrawal of consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal. It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.

This means that we need to be able to provide the individual the chance to withdraw their consent at any time and it should be as easy as giving this. Therefore, do we have an opportunity on the driver sign-up page to return and also “untick” such box for example?

3. *Consent text*
I propose the following text for the consent. We can amend the exact wording, but it is important that it covers:
- the purposes for which the data will be processed
- the type of data that will be processed
- identity of the organisation processing data
- possibility to withdraw the consent

You have identified that you don’t have a vehicle yet. Bolt works with our trusted Fleet Partners* who would like to contact you and offer their cooperation opportunities. 
/ / Yes, I would like to share my contact details (name, e-mail, phone number) for the purpose described above with Bolt’s Fleet Partners. 
_You can withdraw your consent at any time by … . The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal._ 

*Can we refer to the list of Fleet Partners who we would providing the data?

Liis

Query that joins all searches to driver prices in prediction & matching phases:



{noformat}with searches as (
	select sdv.search_categories_overview__created as created,
		sdv.search_categories_overview__user_id as user_id,
		sdv.search_categories_overview__city_id as city_id,
		sdv.search_categories_overview_category__search_category_id as search_category_id,
		sdv.price_prediction_result__price_prediction_token as price_prediction_token,
	    sdv.price_prediction_result_rate__predicted_price as predicted_price,
		sdv.company_order__id as order_id,
		sdv.company_order_try__driver_id as driver_id,
		case when sdv.company_order__state = 'finished' then 1 else 0 end as order_finished
	from etl_search_denormalized_view sdv
	where sdv.search_categories_overview__created >= '2022-02-07 00:00:00'::timestamp
		and sdv.price_prediction_result__price_prediction_token is not NULL
)

select s.*,
	pprr.predicted_price,
	pprr.surge_multiplier,
	pprr.created,
	pprr.driver_prices,
	dpsd.driver_prices as matching_driver_prices
from searches s
left join ext_pricing.price_prediction_result_rate pprr on pprr.price_prediction_token = s.price_prediction_token
	and pprr.search_category_id = s.search_category_id
	and pprr.created_hour >= '2022-02-07 00:00:00'::timestamp
left join ext_pricing.driver_pricing_select_drivers dpsd on dpsd.order_id = s.order_id
	and dpsd.city_id = s.city_id
	and dpsd.created_hour >= '2022-02-07 00:00:00'::timestamp
limit 100;{noformat}

{quote}_I understand your question. It is quite complex issue, and I probably did not entirely clarify the situation in the previous email._ 

_When I mentioned dept and profit - I meant it in bookkeeping sense._  

_Reserves and the share capital are similar. For example, share capital is always in the same amount, although it is being spent, i.e. the company buys certain assets for that amount. The same thing is with reserves._

_Currently, the Croatian company has debt to the Estonian founder on account of a loan in the amount of EUR 200,000.00. This debt is now recorded in the business records as a debt, i.e. deficit._

_The Estonian founder has the right to waive that claim by turning it into capital reserves. Once this has been done, the Croatian company shall no longer have debt to the founder, but this amount will be recorded as reserves, regardless of the fact that amount has been spent- Everything the Croatian company has bought for that amount is worth EUR 200,000.00 in the business records._

_In the event that one day the accounting assets are in deficit, the company can cover this deficit from these reserves. By cover I mean to book the amount transferred from the reserve to the assets and thus become solvent again._

_If the Croatian company will not have any deficit in the assets, the founder as shareholder will be able decide to pay out these reserved to himself (the extra amount after all depts to any creditor is settled)_

_It similar in respect of the share capital increase - the founder can enter its claim in the share capital and thereby increase the share capital although the money that has been loaned has already been spent._ 

_The difference with reserves is that the memorandum of association does not have to be amended, but such transfer to reserves is recorded only in the business records of the company._

_To sum up -  This means, the entry of the loan in the reserves is not affected by the fact whether the amount has already been spent or not. The company will delete the debt to the founder only from one part of the balance sheet and simultaneously record this amount in the capital reserves. Also, the fact that the company will never have a debt (at the end of the year) also has not effect. Unless it has a debt, the founder can pay out this amount to himself or leave the amount in the reserves until any such time that he wishes._{quote}

{code:sql}WITH _booking_item AS (
SELECT
booking_id,
SUM(booked_amount) AS booked_amount,
listagg(payment_method_id,',') AS payment_method_id,
CASE WHEN POSITION('card' IN listagg(payment_method_type,','))>0 THEN 'card' WHEN POSITION('cash' IN listagg(payment_method_type,','))>0 THEN 'cash' ELSE 'bolt_credit' END AS payment_method_type,
SUM(CASE WHEN payment_method_type LIKE 'card%' THEN captured_amount ELSE NULL END) AS card_captured_amount,
SUM(CASE WHEN payment_method_type = 'cash' THEN captured_amount ELSE NULL END) AS cash_captured_amount,
SUM(CASE WHEN payment_method_type = 'bolt_credit' THEN captured_amount ELSE NULL END) AS bolt_credit_captured_amount,
SUM(CASE WHEN payment_method_type = 'bolt_credit' THEN booked_amount ELSE NULL END) AS bolt_credit_booked_amount,
MAX(CASE WHEN payment_method_type LIKE 'card%' THEN state ELSE NULL END) AS card_booked_state
FROM balance_user.balance_user_booking_item
WHERE created BETWEEN '2022-01-27' AND '2022-02-08 00:00:00'
GROUP BY 1
),
_payment_problem AS (
SELECT
payment_id,
created,
state,
RANK () OVER (PARTITION BY payment_id ORDER BY created DESC) AS rnk
FROM fraud_user_payment_problem
WHERE created>='2022-01-27'
AND state<>'ignored'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
)
SELECT DISTINCT
doo.country AS country,
doo.city_id,
doo.id AS order_id,
doo.created,
doo.master_user_id AS user_id,
ROUND((bi.booked_amount / r.rate), 4) AS user_price_eur,
CASE WHEN bi.bolt_credit_booked_amount = bub.booking_amount_total THEN 'bolt_credit' ELSE COALESCE(p.payment_method_type, bi.payment_method_type) END AS payment_method_type,
CASE WHEN bi.bolt_credit_booked_amount = bub.booking_amount_total THEN 'bolt_credit' ELSE bi.payment_method_type END AS payment_method_group,
bub.fraud_result AS booking_fraud_result,
bub.capture_amount_total,
bub.uncovered_amount,
bi.bolt_credit_captured_amount,
CASE WHEN pp.payment_id IS NOT NULL OR pr."type"='chargeback' OR bub.uncovered_amount*1.0/bi.booked_amount>=0.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS bad_payment,
DATEDIFF('day',u.created,doo.created) as user_age,
--CASE WHEN pmu.card_country<>doo.country THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS foreign_card,
--DATEDIFF('day',pmu.created,doo.created) as card_age,
NULLIF(json_extract_path_text(fra.input, 'additional', 'related_bookings_info', 'total', 'user_failed_booking_count', true),' ')::int as user_failed_booking_count,
NULLIF(json_extract_path_text(fra.input, 'additional', 'related_bookings_info', 'total', 'user_failed_booking_sum_eur', true), ' ')::float as user_failed_booking_sum_eur,
frad.user_device_created_age_in_days
FROM delivery.delivery_order_order AS doo
LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_user_basket AS oub ON oub.user_id = doo.master_user_id AND oub.order_id = doo.id
LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_basket_user_basket_booking AS ubb ON oub.user_basket_id = ubb.user_basket_id AND ubb.city_id = oub.city_id
LEFT JOIN balance_user.balance_user_billing_transaction AS bt ON ubb.id = bt.source_id AND ubb.city_id=bt.source_city_id AND bt.transaction_reason_type='booking'
LEFT JOIN balance_user.balance_user_booking AS bub ON bt.id = bub.transaction_id
LEFT JOIN _booking_item AS bi ON bi.booking_id = bub.id
LEFT JOIN payment_payment_order AS ppo ON ppo.order_id = bub.id AND ppo.type = 'balance'
LEFT JOIN payment_payment AS p ON p.payment_order_id = ppo.id
LEFT JOIN payment_payment_row AS pr ON pr.id=p.last_payment_row_id
--LEFT JOIN payment_payment_method_user AS pmu ON pmu.payment_method_id=p.payment_method_id AND pmu.payment_user_id=ppo.payment_user_id AND pmu.payment_method_type=p.payment_method_type
LEFT JOIN _payment_problem AS pp ON pp.payment_id=p.id AND pp.rnk=1
LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r ON doo.currency = r.currency AND date_trunc('day', doo.created) = date_trunc('day',r.valid_on)
LEFT JOIN pii.etl_archive_analytical_delivery_order_request_calculation AS fra ON fra.order_id=ubb.id AND fra.city_id=ubb.city_id
LEFT JOIN pii.etl_archive_analytical_delivery_order_request_data AS frad ON frad.order_user_basket_booking_id=ubb.id AND frad.city_id=ubb.city_id
LEFT JOIN pii.user_user AS u ON u.id=doo.master_user_id
WHERE doo.created BETWEEN '2022-01-27' AND '2022-02-08 00:00:00'
AND (bi.card_booked_state != 'needs_token' OR bi.card_booked_state IS NULL)
AND doo.state = 'delivered'
AND bub.state = 'captured'
AND bt.source_type = 'delivery'
AND payment_method_group='cash'
AND user_failed_booking_count>0
--AND user_failed_booking_sum_eur>0
ORDER BY doo.id{code}

Hi [~accountid:5f896ba356eec000768527be] \!

Few concerns came up when reviewing the DPA, especially regarding the scope of the data and processing activities for that we would be deemed as a controller under the DPA. 

# *In clause 2.1 the categories of the personal data* that the processor will process on our behalf include:

* usage data (e.g. interests, access times, log data).
* Meta/communication data (e.g. device IDs, IP addresses, location data). 

These do not seem as the data categories for which we would be deemed as controller. If the service provider is processing such data for their own purposes, then they are in the controller position. 
+Please ask Localyze to remove these two categories from clause 2.1.+ 

*2. In clause 2.2 the purposes of the data processing includes data analysis*. If the service provider conducts any data analysis for their own purposes, then they should be the controller of such processing activity. 
+Please ask Localyze to remove this purpose (data analysis) from clause 2.2.+ 

3. Under GDPR the processor should notify us about a data breach. Right now this is not included. +Please ask Localyze to add clauses 4.8 and 4.9 as following:+ 
4.8 The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay after becoming aware of (and in any event within 24 hours of discovering) any accidental or unlawful leakage, destruction, loss, alteration or unauthorised disclosure or access to any Personal Data ("Data Breach"). The Processor will notify the Controller on e-mail addresses [privacy@bolt.eu|mailto:privacy@bolt.eu] and [security@bolt.eu|mailto:security@bolt.eu].

4.9 The Processor will take all commercially reasonable measures to secure the Personal Data, to limit the effects of any Data Breach, and to assist the Controller in meeting the Controller's obligations under applicable law.

*4. According to p 9.2 the controller shall pay any costs incurred by the destruction of the data*. This does not seem reasonable, since the processor shall delete the data they are processing on our behalf when the agreement is terminated and without any costs. 
Please ask Localyze to replace the clauses 9.1 and 9.2 with the following:

9.1 The Processor will only process Personal Data for the term of the DPA. The term of this DPA shall coincide with the commencement of the Main Agreement and this DPA shall terminate automatically together with termination or expiry of the Main Agreement.

9.2 The Processor shall at the choice of the Controller, upon receipt of a written request received within 30 days the end of the provision of the Solution and Services relating to processing, delete or return Personal Data to the Controller. The Processor shall in any event delete all copies of Personal Data in its systems within 3 months of the effective date of termination of the DPA.

Since in full refunds the full amount of the payment is refunded, the previous debt in the rider’s balance will be indicated in the rider’s balance again as debt after we issue a full refund. You understood it correctly. As a matter of fact, the rider will have to pay this same amount once more, causing an overcharge in VAT. 

When it comes to point 1 – no, the rider had 2 unpaid orders, one of 8 AZN and the second one of 2 AZN in this case, while we had to refund the 2 AZN trip only. 

# The rider pays 10 AZN for 2 trips combined (8+2 AZN) - it makes an overall of 11.8 with VAT. 
# We refund the full amount in the order of 2 AZN, and only 10 AZN is refunded to the rider’s balance and it became 8 AZN negative for the previous ride. 
# While paying for the additional debt, 8 AZN, the rider will pay additional VAT now, which will make a total payment amount of 9.44 AZN, and overall 1.44 AZN overcharge in VAT.

# Hard block and schedule blocks are different things. They’re independent. In the example you shared, the driver is hard blocked (partner is blocked) and he’s also with an infinite schedule block, but those are independent. The partner blocked prevents the driver from logging in completely and I believe is also used by OPS when the driver signs up with a different fleet. They check for duplicates and if the driver is hard blocked, they are supposed to prevent new accounts from being created. The schedule blocked, however, doesn’t prevent log in. They can log in, contact Support, if the block is ending in 14 days, they’ll see the date, and so on. It’s a different thing :) 

The device not being hard blocked, it’s also not relevant. We only hard block devices for some specific situations, driver impersonation, for example.

I’ve taken a look at geo areas to target for the first experiment. I took Bucharest and looked at previous 2 weeks of surge and unfulfilled sessions in h3 cells and 10 min time bins. I’ve chosen the areas by  unfulfilled sessions as it correlates well (~0.8) with uplift in rides as measured in previous analysis.

[See how the geo campaign areas would look like from the driver’s perspective HERE|http://datascience.internal/driver_campaigns/ppz/bucharest_visual_10d_20s_3bins.html].

* Filters used: surge in >=10 out of 14 days, >= 20 unfulfilled sessions, each area present for >= 30 minutes

More details in [this notebook|http://datascience.internal/driver_campaigns/ppz/experiment-cells-and-times-Bucharest.html].



Filter definitions:

* Surge & unfulfilled sessions present on at least 10 out of 14 days in (cell, time bin) pair
** To avoid areas with inconsistent surge.
* At least 20 unfulfilled sessions in (cell, time bin) pair
** To avoid areas with low demand as it hurts market if lots of drivers reposition
* Each cell is shown for least 30 minutes
** To improve driver experience by making it more predictable - areas won’t change very quickly



Next steps:

* Driver population for experiment - can we access real-time surge & driver state?
** If not, we could still enrol small % of all driver population and measure repositioning probability conditional on surge & state in post-analysis.
